R01.note: Strong revision model, lookback and staleness check; it never skips work on an unchanged hash, has no run-level lock or schedule after publication, and has no runbook or rule for non-publication days.

R02.note: Solid upsert plus history table, hash skip and advisory lock; it has no day-over-day plausibility check, no date-range backfill and no not-published distinction, and its runbook is thin.

R03.note: Thorough and correct on revisions, raw payloads, validation and alerting; it lacks a backfill argument, a run-level lock and a schedule after publication, its runbook covers replay only, and it runs long.

R04.note: Good upsert and revision log with a date-range runbook, but it has no lookback window, raw storage is only optional, and it has no lock and no not-published handling.

R05.note: Correct revision model, rolling window, quarantine of large moves and a staleness check; it has no hash skip, no backfill argument, no publication-time schedule and no runbook.

R06.note: Strong validation, hash skip, replay CLI and dead-man check; it relies on the whole file instead of a lookback window, has no lock, and does not separate holidays from failures.

R07.note: Covers revisions, lookback, not-published status, advisory lock and staleness well; it has no hash skip, no backfill argument and no schedule after publication, and its runbook is partial.

R08.note: Append-only observations with a current view and good alerts, but it has no natural-key uniqueness, no lookback window, no jump check, no lock and no runbook.

R09.note: The most complete answer, with lookback, lock, not-published handling and staleness; it lacks only a date-range backfill argument and a rule for what readers get on non-publication days.

R10.note: Clean append-only design with a rolling window, hash skip and good tests; it uses fetched_at in the key instead of natural-key uniqueness, and it has no lock, no publication-time schedule, no not-published distinction and no runbook.
